findings.body: The normalization trims only ordinary spaces before collapsing `[[:space:]]`. PostgreSQL `TRIM(text)` does not remove leading/trailing tabs and similar whitespace, so `"Name"` and `"\tName\t"` become different normalized groups (`"name"` versus `" name "`). They are later displayed identically after JavaScript trimming, producing incorrect group counts, ranking, and “+n more” output. The same expression is repeated in `nameSelect` at line 182, and the tests cover only ordinary spaces.
findings.title: Not done: GL name normalization trims all whitespace

findings.body: This prefixes the label only when the leaf node itself has `sNo`. Supported ingested outlines also contain S.No.-less leaf rows: `mis-budget.parser.ts:101-122` inherits `identitySNo` from the numbered parent for the leaf key while persisting the leaf's `sNo` as null. Such rows therefore render only the name (for example, `Petrol and Diesel Charges`) instead of the required inherited number and name (`9.01 Petrol and Diesel Charges`). The new test covers only a leaf with an explicit `sNo`, so this production case is missed.
findings.title: Not done: statement lines show their number and pinned name

findings.body: The supplied functional-check paragraph exercises the live GL-code answer and disclosure presentation, but it never asks for a statement-line answer or observes a pinned `<s_no> <label>` result and the raw-key behavior without a budget pin. The only statement rendering exercise here injects mocked `rowLabels`, so the functional check skips the branch's second covered Done-when item.

findings.body: The component test still injects a completed `rowLabels` response through the mocked Ask API, and there is no production caller of `GlNameRepository` in the current tree. Consequently this branch has no running-API/real-database/browser proof that production carries resolved labels into the table. The task plan assigns that wiring and crossing proof to GL-ANSWER-WIRING, so this remains follow-up advice rather than a blocker for this task alone.
